title: Build a game console chip inside an AI model, just for fun
summary: Drew Breunig asked Claude Opus to bake a Nintendo console processor into a small Qwen model; Super Mario Bros now runs, very slowly, inside it.
agent_role: Opus researched the method, found 15-year-old processor tests, and built the model weights and a command-line player. Drew gave two short prompts.
outcome: Simon Willison reports NES games like Super Mario Bros run, very slowly, inside the model.
what_they_did: Drew Breunig pointed Opus at an article about running a computer inside a model's weights. He asked whether a Nintendo console chip could be emulated this way. Then he told it to build the weights and a command-line tool that runs a game file.
how_it_went: According to Simon Willison's write-up, it works and plays Super Mario Bros very slowly. Opus found and used a public set of processor tests to check its work.
worth_knowing: The agent leaned on an existing set of conformance tests, which gave it a clear way to check correctness.
prompt: Read [article URL] and any related source code. Then explore whether this technique could emulate [old hardware]. Estimate what model size it would need. If it looks feasible, propose a build plan using existing test suites to check correctness, and wait for my go-ahead before building.

curation.rationale: A novel build driven by two prompts, with the code public and conformance tests found by the agent. It reaches us through an aggregator post with few details.
